blocks.prompt: 9 A particle moves along a circular path, described by the position vector \(\mathbf{r}(t) = R\cos\omega t\,\hat{i} + R\sin\omega t\,\hat{j}\). Prove that its velocity is perpendicular to its position vector.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh proof (saboot) wala sawal hai. Do non-zero vectors tab perpendicular (aapas mein \(90^{\circ}\)) hote hain jab un ka dot product zero ho.
Diya kya hai? Circle par chalte particle ka \(\mathbf{r}(t) = R\cos\omega t\,\hat{i} + R\sin\omega t\,\hat{j}\).
Saabit kya karna hai? \(\mathbf{v}(t)\) aur \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) perpendicular hain.
Plan: chain rule se \(\mathbf{v}(t)\) nikalo, phir \(\mathbf{r}\cdot\mathbf{v}\) nikal kar dikhao ke yeh har \(t\) par zero hai, aur yeh bhi ke koi vector zero nahin.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = R\cos\omega t\,\hat{i} + R\sin\omega t\,\hat{j}\); \(R\) aur \(\omega\) non-zero constants hain.
Saabit karna: \(\mathbf{v}(t) \perp \mathbf{r}(t)\).
Tareeqa: \(\mathbf{r}\cdot\mathbf{v} = 0\) dikhana, aur yeh ke dono vectors zero nahin.

Velocity
\[\mathbf{v}(t) = -R\omega\sin\omega t\,\hat{i}\]
\[\quad + R\omega\cos\omega t\,\hat{j}\]
Kyun: chain rule: \(\cos\omega t\) ka derivative \(-\omega\sin\omega t\) aur \(\sin\omega t\) ka \(\omega\cos\omega t\). Andar wale \(\omega t\) ka derivative \(\omega\) bahar aata hai.
Dhyan dein: yeh \(\omega\) bhool jana aam ghalti hai.

Dot product
\[\mathbf{r}\cdot\mathbf{v} = (R\cos\omega t)(-R\omega\sin\omega t)\]
\[\quad + (R\sin\omega t)(R\omega\cos\omega t)\]
\[= -R^{2}\omega\sin\omega t\cos\omega t\]
\[\quad + R^{2}\omega\sin\omega t\cos\omega t\]
\[= 0\]
Kyun: dot product mein \(\hat{i}\) wale hisse aapas mein aur \(\hat{j}\) wale hisse aapas mein multiply kar ke jama karte hain. Dono terms barabar magar ulte sign ke hain, is liye cancel ho gaye.

Koi vector zero nahin
\[|\mathbf{r}| = \sqrt{R^{2}\cos^{2}\omega t + R^{2}\sin^{2}\omega t}\]
\[= |R|\]
\[|\mathbf{v}| = |R\omega| \ne 0\]
Kyun: \(\cos^{2} + \sin^{2} = 1\), aur \(R \ne 0\), \(\omega \ne 0\). Yeh qadam zaroori hai, kyunke zero vector ka dot product to har vector ke saath zero hota hai; is liye pehle yaqeen karna parta hai ke dono vectors asal hain.

Nateeja aur tasdeeq
Is liye har lamhe \(\mathbf{v}(t) \perp \mathbf{r}(t)\): velocity circle ke tangent ke saath hai, aur circle ka tangent hamesha radius ke perpendicular hota hai (yeh geometry se bhi aap jaante hain). Ek line ka check: \(|\mathbf{r}|^{2} = \mathbf{r}\cdot\mathbf{r} = R^{2}\) constant hai, to differentiate karne se \(2\,\mathbf{r}\cdot\mathbf{r}' = 0\). Yani jo cheez origin se hamesha ek hi faasle par rahe, us ki velocity hamesha radius ke perpendicular hoti hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\mathbf{r}\cdot\mathbf{v} = 0\) aur \(\mathbf{r} \ne \mathbf{0}\), \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\), is liye har lamhe velocity position vector ke perpendicular hai (yani circle ka tangent hai).

blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 11.3 ke jawab chhape hue nahin hain (Unit 11 ki kisi exercise ke jawab kitab mein nahin hain). Is page ka har jawab hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam hal kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\) jaise angles radians mein hain, is liye calculator RAD mode mein rakhein. Apna hal yahan wale hal se mila kar dekhiye.
